channel.title: RateLog changelog
channel.description: Every AI coding tool pricing and usage-limit change RateLog has caught, dated and sourced.

item.title: Claude Code — Sonnet 5 API pricing made permanent
item.description: [↑ improved] Anthropic made Claude Sonnet 5's introductory API price ($2/$10 per million input/output tokens) permanent, canceling a scheduled increase to $3/$15 that was set for 2026-09-01.

item.title: ChatGPT / Codex — Free-tier chat cap removed
item.description: [↑ improved] GPT-5.6 Luna became the default Free-tier model, and OpenAI began removing the numeric cap on Free-tier text chats entirely, moving toward "unlimited" (subject to abuse guardrails).

item.title: JetBrains AI Assistant — Org credits extended to 12-month validity
item.description: [↑ improved] Announced transitioning org/business AI licensing from fixed seat quotas toward on-demand credits with validity extended from 30 days to 12 months, rolling out through July–August 2026.

item.title: Cline — Launched ClinePass
item.description: [changed] Cline's first-ever direct paid subscription ($9.99/mo) for curated, discounted open-weight-model access — layered on top of the still-free, still-BYOK core product.

item.title: Gemini CLI / Code Assist — Free individual access ended entirely
item.description: [↓ reduced] Gemini CLI and the Code Assist IDE extensions stopped serving requests for the free individual tier and for Google AI Pro/Ultra subscribers — ending free access entirely for individuals, who must now use the successor "Antigravity CLI" or their own paid API key.

item.title: Kiro — Added Pro Max tier
item.description: [↑ improved] AWS introduced a $100/mo Pro Max tier (5,000 credits) to bridge the gap between Pro+ ($40) and Power ($200), giving mid-heavy users a predictable flat rate instead of unpredictable overage charges.

item.title: Devin Desktop (formerly Windsurf) — Rebranded to "Devin Desktop"
item.description: [changed] Cognition rebranded the Windsurf IDE as “Devin Desktop,” unifying it with the cloud agent Devin under one product and opening it to third-party agents via the open Agent Client Protocol.

item.title: GitHub Copilot — Flat premium-request quotas replaced with AI Credits
item.description: [changed] GitHub replaced its flat monthly Premium Request quotas (e.g. 300/month for Pro) with a token-consumption-based "AI Credits" system (1 credit = $0.01) across all plans, and introduced a new top individual tier, Copilot Max, at $100/month. Total credit allowances ended up higher than sticker price once bonus credits are included, but billing is now metered rather than a flat predictable count.

item.title: Cursor — Teams split into two seat tiers
item.description: [↑ improved] Standard keeps its $40/seat price but gains materially more included usage, split into first-party and third-party model pools. A new $120/seat Premium tier (5× Standard’s usage) was added for heavy daily users.

item.title: Warp — BYOK extended to Free tier
item.description: [↑ improved] Bring-your-own-API-key support was extended to all plans including Free, letting Free users route requests through their own keys instead of being limited to the onboarding credit grant.

item.title: Gemini CLI / Code Assist — Google AI Ultra price cut (no longer grants CLI quota)
item.description: [changed] Google cut the Google AI Ultra subscription price from $249.99/mo to $99.99/mo (5× Pro usage), adding a $199.99/mo tier (20× Pro usage) — though after June 18 this subscription no longer grants any Gemini CLI quota at all.

item.title: Claude Code — Weekly limits raised 50%
item.description: [↑ improved] One week after the 5-hour doubling, Anthropic raised weekly Claude Code usage limits by 50% for Pro, Max, and Team plans. Framed as promotional, it has been extended repeatedly and is confirmed live through August 31, 2026.

item.title: Claude Code — 5-hour limits doubled
item.description: [↑ improved] Anthropic doubled Claude Code's 5-hour rate limits for Pro, Max, and Team plans (permanent) and removed a peak-hour usage reduction, enabled by new compute capacity from a deal giving Anthropic access to SpaceX's Colossus 1 data center.

item.title: Amazon Q Developer — Product sunset announced
item.description: [↓ reduced] AWS announced Amazon Q Developer’s IDE plugins and paid Pro subscription are being sunset in favor of a new agentic IDE, "Kiro" — new Free Tier and Pro signups blocked from May 15, 2026, full end of support April 30, 2027.

item.title: ChatGPT / Codex — Business seat price cut
item.description: [↑ improved] Cut ChatGPT Business per-seat price about $5: from $30/mo ($25 annual) down to $25/mo ($20 annual).

item.title: ChatGPT / Codex — Codex switched to token-based credits
item.description: [changed] Switched Codex from flat per-message billing to token-based credits at API rates for Plus, Pro, and Business — cost now scales with tokens used instead of one flat unit per task.

item.title: Devin Desktop (formerly Windsurf) — Flat credits replaced with daily/weekly quotas; Pro price up
item.description: [↓ reduced] Cognition replaced flat monthly credit-pool billing with a token-based system giving daily + weekly usage allowances, raised Pro from $15→$20/mo and Teams from $30→$40/seat/mo (both reportedly grandfathered for existing subscribers), and launched a new $200/mo Max tier.

item.title: Replit Agent — New Pro plan replaces Teams
item.description: [↑ improved] Discontinued the separate Teams plan for a new $100/mo Pro plan with 1-month credit rollover and up to 15 collaborators; Core's annual price dropped to $20/mo with 5 collaborators built in.

item.title: Warp — Legacy tiers collapsed into one $20/mo plan
item.description: [↓ reduced] Collapsed three legacy paid tiers (Pro, Turbo, Lightspeed) into a single $20/mo Build plan; independent analysis characterized this as a net price increase for many existing $10–15/mo subscribers, even though per-unit overage pricing improved and BYOK access was added.

item.title: Cline — First paid organizational tiers
item.description: [changed] Introduced Teams and Enterprise tiers after previously having no paid tier of any kind beyond BYOK inference costs.

item.title: Zed — Moved from flat prompt limits to metered billing
item.description: [changed] Overhauled pricing from flat prompt-count limits to token-based billing. Pro dropped from $20/mo (500 prompts/month) to $10/mo, but the flat allowance was replaced with only $5/mo of included credit plus usage-based overage at API list price + 10%.

item.title: Claude Code — Weekly limits introduced for the first time
item.description: [↓ reduced] Anthropic stacked a new 7-day usage cap on top of the existing 5-hour window, citing 24/7 automated usage and account sharing/reselling by under 5% of subscribers. This was the structural change that created the current two-window system.

item.title: JetBrains AI Assistant — Quotas tied to plan price, shrinking for heavy users
item.description: [↓ reduced] Replaced its opaque per-plan quota with a rule that each plan's AI-Credit allowance equals its USD price (plus a small bonus on Ultimate). JetBrains acknowledged quotas were shrinking for a meaningful share of users, especially heavy Junie agent users, since old quotas had been set unsustainably high as a promotional measure.

item.title: Cursor — Teams moved to usage-based billing
item.description: [changed] Teams moved from a fixed per-request cost (250 included requests/month/seat, $0.08 per extra request) to variable, API-rate usage billing.

item.title: Kiro — Emergency usage caps and a signup waitlist
item.description: [↓ reduced] Days after Kiro's public preview launched, AWS imposed temporary daily usage caps and a signup waitlist due to overwhelming demand — lifted in October 2025 when the current credit-tier system replaced it.

item.title: Replit Agent — Switched to effort-based billing
item.description: [changed] Replaced flat $0.25-per-checkpoint billing with effort-based pricing, where each checkpoint's cost scales with the actual compute the Agent used.

item.title: Cursor — Pro moved off flat "500 fast requests"
item.description: [changed] Cursor dropped the old flat ‘500 fast requests/month’ Pro model for usage-based pricing: Pro now includes at least $20/month of inference at API prices and unlimited use of the 'Auto' model. Also launched the $200/month Ultra tier.
